persona: Dana, owner of a two-location bakery
goal: Make an Excel spreadsheet for my two-location bakery to track weekly sales. One row per day (Monday to Sunday), columns for Downtown sales, Midtown sales, a Total column that uses a SUM formula, and a weekly total row at the bottom with SUM formulas. Fill in realistic sample numbers. Save it as {dir}\bakery-sales.xlsx

Write a Python script for my roofing company that estimates a roof job. It takes square feet and roof pitch (low, medium, steep) as command line arguments, adds 10 percent waste, prices shingles at $4.25 per square foot with a pitch multiplier (1.0, 1.2, 1.5), and prints a clear estimate. When run with no arguments it should print an example estimate for 2000 square feet, medium pitch. Use only the Python standard library. Save it as {dir}\roof_estimate.py

Make a CSV file of 20 sample real estate leads for a follow-up schedule with these columns: name, phone, lead source, price range, last contact date, next follow-up date, notes. Use made-up names and 555 phone numbers. Save it as {dir}\leads-followup.csv

Build a one-page website for a small independent insurance agency in Sacramento: a headline, three cards for auto, home and life insurance, a short about section, and a contact form with name, phone and email. One self-contained HTML file with the CSS inside, mobile friendly. Save it as {dir}\insurance-landing.html

persona: Leo, runs IT for a small office
goal: Write a PowerShell script that zips a folder into a backup file named with today's date (like Backup-2026-10-30.zip) inside a destination folder, keeps only the 7 newest backups, and prints what it did. Parameters: -Source and -Destination. Save it as {dir}\backup.ps1

Write a small Node.js program that splits a night's tip pool among staff by hours worked. Put the logic in tipsplit.js exporting splitTips(totalTips, staff) where staff is a list of {name, hours}, and amounts are rounded to cents and add up exactly to the total. Also write tipsplit.test.js using node:assert that tests it and prints 'All tests passed.'. Save both files in {dir}

Write three short patient appointment reminder messages for a dental office: one text message (under 160 characters), one email, and one reminder for patients who missed their last cleaning. Friendly, plain words, with placeholders like [Patient Name] and [Date]. Save them as {dir}\dental-reminders.md

Write a Python script that reads an invoices CSV (columns: client, invoice_number, amount, paid as yes or no) and prints each client's unpaid total and the grand total unpaid. Also create a sample invoices.csv with 12 rows. When run, the script reads invoices.csv from its own folder. Use only the standard library. Save both files in {dir} as invoice_totals.py and invoices.csv

Make an Excel spreadsheet release plan for a new single: a task list from 6 weeks before release to 2 weeks after (artwork, distributor upload, pre-save link, TikTok teasers, playlist pitching, release day posts, follow-up), with columns for task, due date, owner, status and a days-until-due column that uses a formula based on TODAY(). Save it as {dir}\single-release-plan.xlsx

Make a 4-week beginner workout plan for a personal training client as a Word document: three workouts a week, each with exercises, sets and reps, and a short note on rest. Save it as {dir}\workout-plan.docx
